<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares any personal information of another individual without their consent shall be banned immediately.

<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

#### Art. 10 Alternative accounts
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not use alternative accounts to:\
a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\
b. bypass punishments.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

#### Art. 2. Scope
The Penal Code shall apply to all members of the server.

#### Art. 3. Discord Terms of Service and Community Guidelines
Members of Administration may ensure contents and behaviours comply with Discord's ToS and Community Guidelines, but can only be punished as defined in this Penal Code. For any behaviours or contents that violates Discord ToS or Community Guidelines that are undefined and / or not criminalised in this Penal Code, consult to the Head Administrator or Director.

#### Art. 4. Definitions
<sup>1</sup> For the purposes of this Code, the following terms shall be defined as:\
a. *interactions* means any interaction between members that are:
  1. Text messages;
  2. Voice messages;
  3. Video call;
  4. Livestreams; and / or
  5. Voice call.

b. *media* means any content or visual/auditory that can be perceived, accessed, or viewed by another member.

c. *personal information* means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. This includes but not limited to someone's age, legal name, and home address.

d. *to depict* means to represent, portray, or convey through visual, textual, auditory, or roleplayed means, a person, act, or scenario in a manner that a reasonable member would recognise as representing that person, act, or scenario. This includes but is not limited to:
  1. images, videos, GIFs, or other visual media;
  2. written or narrated descriptions, including roleplay or story-format text;
  3. audio recordings, voice acting, or impersonated sounds; and
  4. AI-generated or edited content representing a real or implied individual.

## Chapter 2: Specific Provisions

### Section 1: Common Behaviours

#### Art. 5 Ping abuse
<sup>1</sup> Ping abuse shall be defined as pinging another member without their consent and that serves no purpose and is purely intended to annoy or harass.

<sup>2</sup> A member repeatedly pinging another member in large amounts shall receive:\
a. a five (5) minute timeout on the first offence;\
b. subsequent offences or more shall raise the duration in minutes by multiplying the last time out duration by 2;\
c. if they persist after their timeout with the duration of 1 week or more, they shall be kicked.

#### Art. 6. Spamming
<sup>1</sup> Spamming is prohibited if it:
a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or
b. the advertiser’s sole intention in the server is to advertise.

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

### Section 2: Accounts and Identity

#### Art. 8 Personal information
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares any personal information of another individual without their consent shall be banned immediately.

#### Art. 9 Impersonation
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

#### Art. 10 Alternative accounts
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not use alternative accounts to:\
a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\
b. bypass punishments.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

### Section 3: Unsolicited Behaviours and Contents

#### Art. 11. Removal of contents
<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall immediately delete any of the contents defined from Article 12 trough 16 that constitutes a violation.

<sup>2</sup> Where the violating content is not directly deletable by an Administrator, they shall instead require the member to remove or change the content within a reasonable timeframe, with failure to comply treated as a continuing violation.

#### Art. 12 Files and links
<sup>1</sup> The sharing of files or other downloadable attachments containing malicious code, malware, viruses, trojans, ransomware, spyware, or keyloggers shall be punishable by an instant ban.

<sup>2</sup> Sharing links, drive folders, or external repositories that directly host or lead to malicious files or phishing pages is treated identically to direct file uploads and has the same punishment defined in paragraph 1.

<sup>3</sup> Files or attachments that are not necessarily harmful but cause temporary disruptions such as temporarily corrupting the rendering of the Discord application, the sender shall be warned. Repeated behaviours shall lead to a timeout. After four counts, the sender shall be kicked.

#### Art. 13 Non-consensual romantic pairings
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not pair, “ship”, or depict real individuals of the server in romantic and / or sexual contexts in any media or interaction, without prior explicit consent from any of the parties involved in the depiction.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a 24-hour timeout on the first offence; and:
b. a kick on the second offence.

<sup>3</sup> Such contents shall be removed upon request by any individuals depicted.

#### Art. 14 Forced feminization and grooming[^1]
<sup>1</sup> Members are prohibited from instructing, coercing, or persistently "encouraging" other members to don specific garments, adopt specific personas, or engage in behaviours that are recognised as elements of sexual roleplay, psychological fetishes, or sexual submissiveness. 

<sup>2</sup> The non-consensual application of behaviours defined in paragraph 1 onto other members shall constitute:
a. a 12-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. a kick on the second offence; and
c. a ban on the third offence.

<sup>3</sup> The presentation of media as a humorous image, macro, trend, or ‘meme’ does not grant exemption from the provisions of this Article.

#### Art. 15 Violence and gore
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not post or have media that depicts:
a. extreme physical violence;
b. real footage of psychological harm;
c. sexual violence;
d. serious bodily injury; and
e. content fetishising these imagery.

<sup>2</sup> Violations of paragraph 1 are punishable by a permanent ban.

<sup>3</sup> The following does not constitute a violation if the sender is using a spoiler tag or in a dedicated NSFW channel:\
a. medias that depict surgical operations in a clinical context;\
b. medias depicting real war footages; and\
c. arts depicting violence and blood.

#### Art. 16 Sexual and suggestive media and interactions
<sup>1</sup> Not Safe for Work, abbreviated as NSFW, shall be defined as anything which includes media or interactions; that is reasonably considered inappropriate, explicit, or intrusive to be viewed, heard, or engaged with in public spaces, workplaces, or shared social and domestic environments without the explicit consent or prior warning of those present.

<sup>2</sup> Members interacting in a way that depicts or implies an explicit sexual act shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 2-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a 4-hour timeout on the third offence; and
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

<sup>3</sup> Members discussing sexual acts, preferences and / or characters or persons in any channel not designated for NSFW contents, shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence to move their discussion to a designated channel for NSFW contents;
b. a 2-hour timeout on their second offence for failure to move their discussion;
c. a 12-hour timeout on their third offence; and
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

<sup>3a</sup> Members discussing the size, girth, dimensions, or other measurements or qualities of genitalia or sexual anatomy, whether their own, another member's, or hypothetical, outside a designated NSFW channel, shall receive the same punishment ladder as paragraph 3.

<sup>4</sup> Members depicting specific gestures, facial expressions, or movements that is otherwise only made during or to represent sexual acts, they shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 4-hour timeout on the second through fourth offences; and
c. a kick on the fifth offence.

<sup>5</sup> Any depiction of explicit sexual acts, nudity, and adult novelties is punishable by:
a. a 24-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a 1-week timeout on the third and fourth offence; and
d. a kick on the fifth offence.

<sup>6</sup> For the purposes of paragraph 4, prohibited depictions include, but are not limited to:
a. masturbation even if clothed;
b. sexual acts even if cropped;
c. presence of fluids that is made for, during and / or as a result of sexual acts;
d. intentional physical contact of sex organs and other organs for sexual pleasure;
e. clothing specifically designed for sexual pleasure;
f. sexual acts done by other species besides humans; and
g. sexual organs clearly visible through clothing.

<sup>7</sup> Media that only includes the following and does not depict anything above does not constitute a violation:
a. adult novelties that do not necessarily have the form of a sex organ; and
b. fine arts depicting nudity.

<sup>8</sup> For fine arts where a significant portion of the medium is nudity, the sender is required to put a spoiler tag or move to a designated NSFW channel. Failure to do this shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. 1-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. 1-day timeout on the third offence; and
d. a kick on the fourth violation.

<sup>9</sup> Members shall not depict any media where the main content or major portions of it are depictions of suggestive closeups of specific body parts including:
a. buttocks;
b. feet;
c. armpits;
d. breast;
e. pelvic or genitalia region; and
f. thighs;

<sup>10</sup> Violation of paragraph 9 shall be punishable by:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 1-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a 48-hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a 1-week timeout on the fourth offence; and
e. a kick on the fifth offence.

#### Art. 17 Incitement[^2]
The incitement, endorsement, or encouragement to commit a violation of law, disrupt or threaten the order, peace, and unity of the server shall be punishable by no less than 1-week timeout and a 6000₣ fine.

#### Art. 18 General member conduct
<sup>1</sup> The explicit disrespect against the death of another member's friend, family member, pet, or significant other shall be punishable by:
a. a 1-week timeout from the first through the third offence; and
b. an indefinite banishment to the Void until the victim forgives them.


[^1]: Adopted unilaterally by The Director on 19 June 2026, in force since 19 June 2026.
[^2]: Adopted unilaterally by The Director on 14 Aug. 2026, in force since 14 Aug. 2026.

# SR 310 — Penal Code

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100). Applies to all server members and members of administration.

## Chapter 1: General Provisions

### Section 1: Scope and Terminology

#### Art. 1. Purpose
The Penal Code shall define the punishments Administrators are required to punish members for violations of the Public Code.

#### Art. 2. Scope
The Penal Code shall apply to all members of the server.

#### Art. 3. Discord Terms of Service and Community Guidelines
Members of Administration may ensure contents and behaviours comply with Discord's ToS and Community Guidelines, but can only be punished as defined in this Penal Code. For any behaviours or contents that violates Discord ToS or Community Guidelines that are undefined and / or not criminalised in this Penal Code, consult to the Head Administrator or Director.

#### Art. 4. Definitions
<sup>1</sup> For the purposes of this Code, the following terms shall be defined as:\
a. *interactions* means any interaction between members that are:
  1. Text messages;
  2. Voice messages;
  3. Video call;
  4. Livestreams; and / or
  5. Voice call.

b. *media* means any content or visual/auditory that can be perceived, accessed, or viewed by another member.

c. *personal information* means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. This includes but not limited to someone's age, legal name, and home address.

## Chapter 2: Specific Provisions

### Section 1: Common Behaviours

#### Art. 5 Ping abuse
<sup>1</sup> Ping abuse shall be defined as pinging another member without their consent and that serves no purpose and is purely intended to annoy or harass.

<sup>2</sup> A member repeatedly pinging another member in large amounts shall receive:\
a. a five (5) minute timeout on the first offence;\
b. subsequent offences or more shall raise the duration in minutes by multiplying the last time out duration by 2;\
c. if they persist after their timeout with the duration of 1 week or more, they shall be kicked.

#### Art. 6. Spamming
<sup>1</sup> Spamming is prohibited if it:
a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or
b. the advertiser’s sole intention in the server is to advertise.

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

### Section 2: Accounts and Identity

#### Art. 8 Personal information
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares any personal information of another individual without their consent shall be banned immediately.

#### Art. 9 Impersonation
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

#### Art. 10 Alternative accounts
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not use alternative accounts to:\
a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\
b. bypass punishments.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

### Section 3: Unsolicited Behaviours and Contents

#### Art. 11. Deletion of contents
<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall immediately delete any of the contents defined from Article 12 trough 16 that constitutes a violation.

#### Art. 12 Files and links
<sup>1</sup> The sharing of files or other downloadable attachments containing malicious code, malware, viruses, trojans, ransomware, spyware, or keyloggers shall be punishable by an instant ban.

<sup>2</sup> Sharing links, drive folders, or external repositories that directly host or lead to malicious files or phishing pages is treated identically to direct file uploads and has the same punishment defined in paragraph 1.

<sup>1</sup> Members shall not pair, “ship”, or depict real individuals of the server in romantic and / or sexual contexts in any media or interaction, without prior explicit consent from any of the parties involved in the depiction.

b. a kick on the second offence.

### Section 1: Scope and Terminology

#### Art. 1. Purpose
The Penal Code shall define the punishments Administrators are required to punish members for violations of the Public Code.

The Penal Code shall apply to all members of the server.

<sup>1</sup> For the purposes of this Code, the following terms shall be defined as:\
a. *interactions* means any interaction between members that are:

  2. Voice messages;
  3. Video call;
  4. Livestreams; and / or
  5. Voice call.

### Section 1: Common Behaviours

#### Art. 5 Ping abuse
<sup>1</sup> Ping abuse shall be defined as pinging another member without their consent and that serves no purpose and is purely intended to annoy or harass.

<sup>2</sup> A member repeatedly pinging another member in large amounts shall receive:\
a. a five (5) minute timeout on the first offence;\
b. subsequent offences or more shall raise the duration in minutes by multiplying the last time out duration by 2;\
c. if they persist after their timeout with the duration of 1 week or more, they shall be kicked.

#### Art. 6. Spamming
<sup>1</sup> Spamming is prohibited if it:
a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or
b. the advertiser’s sole intention in the server is to advertise.

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

### Section 2: Accounts and Identity

#### Art. 8 Personal information
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares personal information of other individuals without their consent shall be banned immediately.

#### Art. 9 Impersonation
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

#### Art. 10 Alternative accounts
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not use alternative accounts to:\
a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\
b. bypass punishments.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

### Section 3: Unsolicited Behaviours and Contents

#### Art. 11. Deletion of contents
<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall immediately delete any of the contents defined from Article 12 trough 16 that constitutes a violation.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:

b. a kick on the second offence.

a. a 12-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. a kick on the second offence; and
c. a ban on the third offence.

<sup>3</sup> The presentation of media as a humorous image, macro, trend, or ‘meme’ does not grant exemption from the provisions of this Article.

#### Art. 15 Violence and gore
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not post or have media that depicts:
a. extreme physical violence;
b. real footage of psychological harm;
c. sexual violence;
d. serious bodily injury; and
e. content fetishising these imagery.

b. medias depicting real war footages; and\

b. a 4-hour timeout on the second through fourth offences; and
c. a kick on the fifth offence.

c. a 1-week timeout on the fourth offence; and

#### Art. 5 Ping Abuse
<sup>1</sup> Ping abuse shall be defined as pinging another member without their consent and that serves no purpose and is purely intended to annoy or harass.

<sup>2</sup> A member repeatedly pinging another member in large amounts shall receive:\
a. a five (5) minute timeout on the first offence;\

<sup>1</sup> Spamming is prohibited if it:
a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or Self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or
b. the advertiser’s sole intention in the server is to advertise.

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

### Section 2: Accounts and Identity

#### Art. 8 Personal Information
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares personal information of other individuals without their consent shall be banned immediately.

#### Art. 9 Impersonation
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

# SR 410 — Administration Codes Compilations
*(Administration Codes)*

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100). Applies to all members of Administration.

---

## Chapter 1: Purpose and Scope

#### Art. 1 Purpose
The Administration Codes and its subsequent laws shall govern the conduct of the Administration and its procedures.

#### Art. 2 Scope
The Administration Codes and its subsequent laws shall apply to all members of Administration, this includes but not limited to all Administrators who holds positions defined in Chapter 2 of the Server Charter (SR 100) and their appointed staff.

## Chapter 2: General Provisions

### Section 1: Definitions and Principles

#### Art. 3 Definitions
<sup>1</sup> In this Code:\
a. *Administrators* means any member of Administration and their appointed staff.

b. *moderation action* means any action taken to enforce rules or handle members, such as warnings, timeouts, kicks, bans, message deletions, thread closing, etc.

#### Art. 4 Principles
<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall enforce all laws equally to all members of the server.

<sup>2</sup> Administrators shall maintain a peaceful, safe, and orderly environment for the server while maintaining a balance for individual liberty.

<sup>3</sup> At normal times, Administrators are encouraged to maintain close relationships with members of the server.

<sup>4</sup> At times of conflict, Administrators must maintain professionalism and emotional distance.

<sup>5</sup> For any loopholes, flaws, or events not specified in any law or procedures, an Administrator must act in good faith to uphold paragraph 1.

<sup>6</sup> Administrators must fully know the law and specified procedures.

<sup>7</sup> A judging authority must raise the punishment for violations done by Administrators of a senior position.

### Section 2: Server Features

#### Art. 5 Server settings
The authority to modify any server settings rests only to the Director.

#### Art. 5a Bots
The authority to add, remove, or modify server bots shall rest only to the Head Administrator and Director.

---

## Chapter 3: Specific Provisions and Compilations

### Section 1: Behaviours

#### Art. 6 Professional conduct
<sup>1</sup> Administrators are to maintain a respectful manner to all members.

<sup>2</sup> Freedom of speech is limited under Art. 9. of the Public Code (SR 210).

<sup>3</sup> Constant use of slurs, harassment and / or tantrum is punishable by:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 7 Abuse of power
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator shall not use their powers and act out for personal gain, out of irritation, pettiness, or sheer spite.

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall result in:
a. a 48-hour timeout on the first offence; and
b. removal from position on the second offence.

#### Art. 8 Negligence
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator is required to act if available and is well aware a violation of law is happening.

<sup>2</sup> Failure to comply with paragraph 1 shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 9 Bribery
Any Administrators that willingly accept any form of compensation by another individual in exchange for administrative influence shall be punished by removal from position and banned from taking any position in Administration.

---

### Section 2: Exercise of Power and Documentation

#### Art. 10 Moderation actions
<sup>1</sup> Any moderation actions or any general acts shall comply with the Penal Code and the law.

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

<sup>3</sup> Other or higher Administrator shall reverse such unlawful moderation decisions and actions immediately.

<sup>4</sup> Actions taken without good faith by administrators that are not explicitly provided for by an enabling law are not exempt from paragraph 1.

#### Art. 11 Documentation of moderation actions
<sup>1</sup> All moderation actions are to be documented based on outlined procedures by the Head Administrator or Director.

<sup>2</sup> Failure to log a moderation action shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 12 Tampering of moderation logs
<sup>1</sup> The tampering, modification to mislead, or deleting moderation logs shall result in:
a. a 48-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. removal from position the second offence.

<sup>2</sup> Moderation logs that are a result of clerical errors is exempt from paragraph 1.

#### Art. 13 Compromised accounts
<sup>1</sup> A user account is considered compromised if it does any of the following:
a. Sends unauthorised, automated, or deceptive communications, including phishing URLs, fraudulent promotional offers, or mass user mentions;
b. Alters profile metadata, display names, or profile picture to impersonate platform support personnel, server staff, or system bots; or
c. Initiates unauthorised administrative modifications, including the creation of rogue webhooks, role privilege escalations, or bulk invite generation.

<sup>2</sup> Upon encountering a user exhibiting behaviours specified in paragraph 1, an Administrator shall ban the user immediately.

#### Art. 14 Celebration of certain events.

# SR 410 — Administration Codes Compilations
*(Administration Codes)*

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Title 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100). Applies to all members of Administration.

---

## Title 1: Purpose and Scope

#### Art. 1 Purpose
The Administration Codes and its subsequent laws shall govern the conduct of the Administration and its procedures.

#### Art. 2 Scope
The Administration Codes and its subsequent laws shall apply to all members of Administration, this includes but not limited to all Administrators who holds positions defined in Title 2 of the Server Charter (SR 100) and their appointed staff.

## Title 2: General Provisions

### Section 1: Definitions and Principles

#### Art. 3 Definitions
<sup>1</sup> In this Code:\
a. *Administrators* means any member of Administration and their appointed staff.

b. *moderation action* means any action taken to enforce rules or handle members, such as warnings, timeouts, kicks, bans, message deletions, thread closing, etc.

#### Art. 4 Principles
<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall enforce all laws equally to all members of the server.

<sup>2</sup> Administrators shall maintain a peaceful, safe, and orderly environment for the server while maintaining a balance for individual liberty.

<sup>3</sup> At normal times, Administrators are encouraged to maintain close relationships with members of the server.

<sup>4</sup> At times of conflict, Administrators must maintain professionalism and emotional distance.

<sup>5</sup> For any loopholes, flaws, or events not specified in any law or procedures, an Administrator must act in good faith to uphold paragraph 1.

<sup>6</sup> Administrators must fully know the law and specified procedures.

<sup>7</sup> A judging authority must raise the punishment for violations done by Administrators of a senior position.

### Section 2: Server Features

#### Art. 5 Server Settings
The authority to modify any server settings rests only to the Director.

#### Art. 6 Bots
The authority to add, remove, or modify server bots shall rest only to the Head Administrator and Director.

---

## Title 3: Specific Provisions and Compilations

### Section 1: Behaviours

#### Art. 6 Professional Conduct
<sup>1</sup> Administrators are to maintain a respectful manner to all members.

<sup>2</sup> Freedom of speech is limited under Art. 9. of the Public Code (SR 210).

<sup>3</sup> Constant use of slurs, harassment and / or tantrum is punishable by:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 7 Abuse of Power
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator shall not use their powers and act out for personal gain, out of irritation, pettiness, or sheer spite.

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall result in:
a. a 48-hour timeout on the first offence; and
b. removal from position on the second offence.

#### Art. 8 Negligence
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator is required to act if available and is well aware a violation of law is happening.

<sup>2</sup> Failure to comply with paragraph 1 shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 9 Bribery
Any Administrators that willingly accept any form of compensation by another individual in exchange for administrative influence shall be punished by removal from position and banned from taking any position in Administration.

---

### Section 2: Exercise of Power and Documentation

#### Art. 10 Moderation Actions
<sup>1</sup> Any moderation actions or any general acts shall comply with the Penal Code and the law.

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

<sup>3</sup> Other or higher Administrator shall reverse such unlawful moderation decisions and actions immediately.

<sup>4</sup> Actions taken without good faith by administrators that are not explicitly provided for by an enabling law are not exempt from paragraph 1.

#### Art. 11 Documentation of Moderation Actions
<sup>1</sup> All moderation actions are to be documented based on outlined procedures by the Head Administrator or Director.

<sup>2</sup> Failure to log a moderation action shall result in:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 12 Tampering of Moderation Logs
<sup>1</sup> The tampering, modification to mislead, or deleting moderation logs shall result in:
a. a 48-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. removal from position the second offence.

<sup>2</sup> Moderation logs that are a result of clerical errors is exempt from paragraph 1.

laws.content:
# SR 415 — Courts and Appeals Proceedings Code

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100). Applies to all members of Administration.

---

## Section 1: Definitions and Principles

### Art. 1: Definitions
In this Code:\
a. *Administrator* means a member of Administration or one of their appointed staff.

b. *defendant* means a natural member being accused of a violation of the Codes or other laws.

c. *ticket* means a designated chat for a particular case.

### Art. 2: Principles
<sup>1</sup> A defendant must be aware of what they are charged and punished for.

<sup>2</sup> No person of judicial authority shall determine a case that they are personally involved in.

## Section 2: Roles

### Art. 3: Judge
<sup>1</sup> The Judge shall be responsible for the final decision if the defendant is guilty and what punishment is legally applicable.

<sup>2</sup> The Judge shall not lower the punishment as a result of harassment or pressure from the defendant or their supporters.

<sup>3</sup> The Secretary shall assume the role of Judge, if they are available within 24-hours. If not, the Head Administrator or Director may assume the role if they are not personally involved in the case.

<sup>4</sup> The Judge may hold someone in contempt of court for disrespecting or derailing court order, and can give a penalty of:
a. a timeout with a maximum duration of 24 hours; and
b. a fine of a maximum of 5000₣; and

### Art. 4: Prosecutor
<sup>1</sup> The Prosecutor shall be responsible for determining Code and law violations and recommend a penalty.

<sup>2</sup> The Head Administrator or Director shall assume the role of Prosecutor if they are not personally involved in the case.

## Section 3: Proceedings

### Art. 5 Initial filing
<sup>1</sup> A person may be reported for violations and a Prosecutor shall file the case and open a ticket within 24-hours.

<sup>2</sup> Violations of the Penal Code by a regular member does not require a case.

<sup>3</sup> The accused person becomes the Defendant in their case.

### Art. 6 Suspension
<sup>1</sup> Suspension is the act of removing an Administrator of administrative powers.

<sup>2</sup> A suspended Administrator shall be stripped of their roles and permissions and shall not affect any decisions of Administration.

<sup>3</sup> An Administrator shall be suspended once substantial evidence of violations are presented.

### Art. 7 Proceedings
<sup>1</sup> The Prosecutor shall look for and present evidence and determine what violation of law the Defendant has committed.

<sup>2</sup> The Defendant may counter their charges with evidence or assertions. The Prosecutor shall look for and present evidence to determine if the assertions are true.

<sup>3</sup> Proceedings shall take place in the case ticket and no other places.

### Art. 8 Ruling
<sup>1</sup> If the Defendant or Prosecutor does not have any more evidence or argument to present, the Judge shall determine their ruling.

<sup>2</sup> The Judge present their ruling in the ticket.

<sup>3</sup> After the Judge present their ruling, their ruling shall be final.

<sup>4</sup> If the Defendant is found guilty they shall be punished as described by the Judge.

## Section 4: Appeals

### Art. 9 Appeals
<sup>1</sup> If a member somehow believes that they are not guilty after their ruling and punishment, they may file an appeal to a Court of Appeals.

<sup>2</sup> To prevent abuse, a member may file an appeal for free, provided they have new evidence. If a member submits an appeal in bad faith or lack of evidence, they may be fined for 1500₣.

<sup>3</sup> Should a member want to file an appeal again after an initial fine, they shall require 2000₣ to do so.

<sup>4</sup> Payment to the Court of Appeals shall be evenly distributed to all workers who handled the case.

<sup>5</sup> Members of a Court of Appeals shall only decline an appeal due to the lack of new evidence. Violation of this paragraph shall result in removal from position.

## Section 5 Court of Appeals

### Art. 10 Court of Appeals
<sup>1</sup> The Secretary shall have to power to lawfully appoint, remove, and oversee members of the Court of Appeals.

<sup>2</sup> The Director may assume the role of a Court of Appeals if no worker of the Court is available.

## Section 6 Miscellaneous

### Art. 11 Clerical errors
<sup>1</sup> If a Prosecutor somehow cited the wrong article, code, or code version with no bad faith, the case shall be reopened for a corrected ruling under the correct citations.

<sup>2</sup> Miscitation under bad faith is punishable by:
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a 1-week timeout and removal from position on the second offence.

laws.content:
# SR 510 — The Dokusai-kun and The Server

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

## Art. 1 Purpose
Dokusai-kun shall be the symbol and Dicktator of the server and its unity.

## Art. 2 Authority
Dokusai-kun remains subjected under the law and the Administration.

## Art. 3 Power
Dokusai-kun may exercise any power that the Administration does not restrict.

## Art. 4 Restriction on Powers
<sup>1</sup> Dokusai-kun shall not give roles to members that holds administrative permissions.

<sup>2</sup> Dokusai-kun shall not give any currency to another member.

<sup>3</sup> Dokusai-kun shall not delete a channel unilaterally.

## Art. 5 Passing the Crown
<sup>1</sup> If Dokusai-kun did not send a message or done an interaction in the last 90-days, the People may do a server-wide vote to replace Dokusai-kun with another member.

<sup>2</sup> Candidates of Dokusai-kun shall not have comitted any grave violations or predatory conduct.

<sup>3</sup> Dokusai-kun may declare to pass the crown onto another person. Said person is not exempt from paragraph 2's restriction.

## Art. 6 Impeachment
<sup>1</sup> Dokusai-kun shall be subject to impeachment.

<sup>2</sup> If 25% of the server's total active natural members are in favour of impeachment, Dokusai-kun shall be removed from position.

laws.content:
# SR 515 — The Kai-Dokusai and The Server

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

## Preamble
In the name of The Cat!

The Director of the Nirleka Studios Discord Server and his remaining sanity,

in order to stir more chaos to the pot within an otherwise stable Server,

does hereby decree:

## Chapter 1: The Kai-Dokusai

### Section 1: Principles

#### Art. 1 Subordination
The Kai-Dokusai is subordinate to the Dokusai-kun.

#### Art. 2 Under law
<sup>1</sup> The Kai-Dokusai remains subjected under the Server Charter (SR 100) and its subsequent laws.

### Section 2: Powers

#### Art. 3 General powers
<sup>1</sup> The Kai-Dokusai shall not exercise power not explicitly defined in this Act.

<sup>2</sup> The Kai-Dokusai may:\
a. change the Server name;\
b. modify channel names;\
c. create new channels; and\
d. host events.

#### Art. 4 Legislation
<sup>1</sup> The Kai-Dokusai shall have legislative power similar to the Director restricted by the bounds of the Server Charter.

<sup>2</sup> The Director holds ultimate legislative power and shall have the power to override the decisions of the Kai-Dokusai.

#### Art. 5 Executive power
<sup>1</sup> The Kai-Dokusai shall not possess executive power.

<sup>2</sup> The Kai-Dokusai however may request a member of the Executive Branch to carry out a lawful order.

## Chapter 2: The Kai-Dokusai and The Server

### Section 1: Power of the Members

#### Art. 6 Election
The Kai-Dokusai shall only be elected by members of the Server by a majority vote if no Kai-Dokusai is currently in seat.

#### Art. 7 Holding the seat
The Kai-Dokusai may remain in power for life until inactivity after 90 days, resignation, or impeachment.

#### Art. 8 Impeachment
The Kai-Dokusai may be impeached by a majority-vote (50% + 1) and removed from position.

laws.content:
# SR 555 — The Culture Code Between the Director and Members of the Nirleka Studios Discord Server

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

### Art. 1 Cat Supremacy
The Cat is our Soupurreme Glorious Leadah.

### Art. 2 The Director
The Director possesses Soupurreme authority delegated by The Cat.

### Art. 3 Anonymity
Everyone shall have the right to anonymity.

### Art. 4 Humanity
Do not be a dick.

### Art. 5 Nuclear power
Nuclear power plants are among the most overcomplicated ways to boil water. Opposing nuclear power is an opposition against The Cat, and is blasphemy.

### Art. 6 Patience
And whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.

### Art. 7 Trolling
Trolling, or in the current era that is also referred to as rage-baiting, shall not be taken seriously. It means they win. Follow Art. 6.

### Art. 8 Balance
<sup>1</sup> Everyone is equally worthless.

<sup>2</sup> Everyone is made from the hands of a single Creator.

<sup>3</sup> A mortal asserting superiority against another mortal on their natural characteristics is transgression against The Cat.

<sup>4</sup> Male and female, female and male, one needs another. One serves a specific purpose. Otherwise, humanity can not exist. To assert superiority over sex is transgression against The Cat.

### Art. 9 A Belief
<sup>1</sup> There is no compulsion in religion.

<sup>2</sup> The power to punish a mortal for a transgression against the Creator rests between the mortal and the Creator.

<sup>3</sup> Surely someone who believes that our Creator smiles on and rewards the deliberate killing and maiming of innocents believes in a cruel creator. That is not, it cannot be, the Creator of Humanity.

<sup>4</sup> Can a mortal truly follow the words of the Creator? Does one mortal's transgression stain the words of the Creator?

laws.title: The Economy Act
laws.content:
# SR 610 — The Economy Act

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

## Section 1: Currency and Issuing Authority

### Art. 1 Currency unit
The currency of the Nirleka Studios Discord server shall be the Nirleka franc. Denoted by `₣` or ***F R A N C S***.

### Art. 2 Issuing authority
<sup>1</sup> The power to manually give money to another member shall be the Director.

<sup>2</sup> The power to remove money from another member for violations of the Codes shall be the Head Administrator and Director.

## Section 2: Income, Transactions, and Fines

### Art. 3 Limitations
Art. 9 of the Administration Codes (SR 410) governs all use of ***F R A N C S*** in the Administration.

### Art. 4 Income
<sup>1</sup> Members shall receive a variable reward of not less than 5 ***F R A N C S*** and not more than 15 ***F R A N C S*** per message sent in a public channel, subject to a minimum interval restriction of one (1) minute between qualifying rewards.

<sup>2</sup> Members serving in the Administration may receive a fixed amount of ***F R A N C S***.

<sup>3</sup> Members serving in the Administration shall not receive ***F R A N C S*** as a reward for moderation actions.

### Art. 5 Transactions
<sup>1</sup> Transactions using the ***F R A N C S*** in any way shall only be restricted within the features of the server.

<sup>2</sup> Violating paragraph 1 shall result in a 16000 ***F R A N C S*** fine and 48-hour timeout.

### Art. 6 Fines
The Administration may codify a fixed fine for violations of the Codes.

# SR 610 — The Economy Act

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

## Section 1: Currency and Issuing Authority

### Art. 1 Currency unit
The currency of the Nirleka Studios Discord server shall be the Nirleka franc. Denoted by `₣` or ***F R A N C S***.

### Art. 2 Issuing authority
<sup>1</sup> The power to manually give money to another member shall be the Director.

<sup>2</sup> The power to remove money from another member for violations of the Codes shall be the Head Administrator and Director.

## Section 2: Income, Transactions, and Fines

### Art. 3 Limitations
Art. 9 of the Administration Codes (SR 410) governs all use of ***F R A N C S*** in the Administration.

### Art. 4 Income
<sup>1</sup> Members shall receive a variable reward of not less than 5 ***F R A N C S*** and not more than 15 ***F R A N C S*** per message sent in a public channel, subject to a minimum interval restriction of one (1) minute between qualifying rewards.

<sup>2</sup> Members serving in the Administration may receive a fixed amount of ***F R A N C S***.

<sup>3</sup> Members serving in the Administration shall not receive ***F R A N C S*** as a reward for moderation actions.

### Art. 5 Transactions
<sup>1</sup> Transactions using the ***F R A N C S*** in any way shall only be restricted within the features of the server.

<sup>2</sup> Violating paragraph 1 shall result in a 16000 ***F R A N C S*** fine and 48-hour timeout.

### Art. 6 Fines
The Administration may codify a fixed fine for violations of the Codes.

laws.title: The Touch Grass Act
laws.content:
# SR 615 — The Touch Grass Act

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

## Section 1: General Provisions

### Art. 1 Definitions
<sup>1</sup> In this Act:\
a. *touch grass* means a natural person being present outdoors, at least roughly 500 meters away from one's home(s).

b. *proof* means any way to prove that one has touched grass. This includes but not limited to, photos, livestreams, or GPS tracking.

## Section 2: Specific Provisions

### Art. 2 Payout for touching grass
<sup>1</sup> Members shall be compensated for providing proof of touching grass.

<sup>2</sup> Proofs dated before August 2026 are invalid.

<sup>3</sup> Members may receive a minimum of 250 to 660 ***F R A N C S*** for proof(s) per 1-hour period.

<sup>4</sup> Members shall not submit a proof that was not taken by them or another individual that was with them.

<sup>5</sup> Members submitting a fake proof shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 1-week timeout and a fine of 1200 ***F R A N C S***.

laws.title: The Corner Act
laws.content:
# SR 620 — The Corner Act

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance to Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 100), by the Director

---

## Section 1: Definitions and Principles

### Art. 1 Definitions
In this Act:\
a. *corner* means a server channel created specifically for a member.

b. *to archive* means putting a channel in the Public Archive category to remain hidden from the public but can be accessed by those who have Archive Access.

### Art. 2 Principles
<sup>1</sup> The owner of a corner reserves the right to talk in that corner and may prohibit other members from interacting in their corner.

<sup>2</sup> Members of Administration are exempt from paragraph 1 if they have reasonable means and intentions.

<sup>3</sup> The People ultimately owns the server and may order the archival of a corner.

<sup>4</sup> A corner shall not be deleted permanently.

### Art. 3 Permanent corners
<sup>1</sup> The following are designated as permanent corners and can not be removed or taxed:\
a. `nirleka-corner`;\
b. `error-corner`; and\
c. `faze-corner`

### Art. 4 Existing corners
For existing corners, the owner of those corners shall pay for their corner tax on 19 August 2026.

## Section 2: Purchasing and Taxing Corners

### Art. 5 Purchasing corners
<sup>1</sup> A member may purchase a new corner or restore their old one for 50400 ***F R A N C S***.

<sup>2</sup> Members who have committed violations of the Codes shall not acquire any corners.

<sup>3</sup> Members who have purchased a corner shall not purchase another corner.

<sup>4</sup> Once a member have purchased a new corner, a corner with their name or nickname followed by `-corner` shall be created, and be put under the Text Channels category.

### Art. 6 Taxation of corners
<sup>1</sup> The Director shall tax all non-permanent corners for 1600 ***F R A N C S*** per week.

<sup>2</sup> The owner of a corner have 48-hours to compensate the tax once rent is due.

<sup>3</sup> If an owner fails to compensate for the tax, the corner shall be archived.
